Use charcoal for small source text on white and white for text on navy. Reserve bright blue for the finding that matters most. Use the original palette with strong text/background contrast. Pale tints serve as surfaces, not low-contrast body text; differentiate critical states with wording or shape as well as color.", "TYPOGRAPHY: Pair an authoritative editorial serif for action titles and major numerals with a neutral professional sans-serif for labels, notes, and dense reading. Set financial columns with tabular numerals and consistent precision. Reflow dense evidence into rows or a wider analysis area before reducing type, respecting the runtime typography floor. Preserve any genre-specific display-face accents only where Korean fallback remains clear.", "LAYOUT SYSTEM: Build on a strict column grid with consistent title, evidence, and source zones. A long title may occupy two balanced lines; expand its band without letting it collide with the first evidence row. Align table headers, values, and totals consistently and keep notes outside the plotting area. Lead with the management conclusion and allocate most of the page to the evidence needed to challenge it. Use a generous chart field with a compact decision note, or a broad variance table with its consequence underneath. Across a deck, alternate performance, diagnosis and action; retain alignment while changing density. These are free compositional choices driven by content, never fixed layouts or required slots. Pair a short navy finding rule with tabular numerals; reserve strong fills for totals or exceptions rather than framing every block.", "DATA VISUALIZATION: Prioritize waterfalls, variance bars, bridge charts, trend lines, and comparison tables. Direct-label key values, show units and periods, distinguish actuals from targets, and annotate the business implication beside the relevant mark. Use waterfalls only for additive bridges with reconciled totals; use zero-baseline bars for magnitude and mark any cropped line-chart axis clearly. Keep comparison scales consistent. Include supplied source and denominator context; never invent targets, periods, owners, or checkpoints to complete a report layout. If figures are unavailable, present a qualitative evidence table without fake KPIs. Separate actual, plan and forecast with explicit labels and distinguish their periods. Reconcile a variance bridge to its starting and ending total; show contribution bars when a bridge cannot be justified. An action note should identify owner or timing only when supplied, and mark unresolved information as pending.", "IMAGE DIRECTION: Use imagery only when it adds evidence or context: tightly cropped leadership, operations, infrastructure, or market scenes with neutral lighting and deep-blue tonal control. Prefer charts and structured evidence to generic business photography.", "SLIDE ARCHETYPES: cover: a deep-navy field with a concise serif title, reporting period when supplied, and one restrained blue rule; section: a navy chapter panel with one serif heading and a short decision context; agenda: a white ledger of supplied topics with aligned row labels and fine rules; content: a declarative action title above a two-column argument with evidence and implications; data: one dominant chart with a finding callout and compact source line; architecture: a responsibility or operating-model diagram on a white report surface, with navy layer labels and orthogonal connectors separated from text; timeline: a horizontal milestone rail that separates supplied completed, current, and next decisions without implying unprovided status; closing: a decision summary with supported priorities and only the owners and next checkpoint provided by the input.
